# Lumiose UI

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

These docs ship in `@lumiose/ui` and match the installed version: `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`.
In a project that depends on it, `lumiose docs ui` prints the index and `lumiose docs dialog` a
component's page; the Lumiose MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists every component's parts,
props, events and styling hooks. The Lumiose docs: `node_modules/lumiose/docs/llms.txt`.

<!-- source: README.md -->

# UI components

> `@lumiose/ui`: accessible, unstyled UI primitives built on native elements (`<dialog>`, popover, invoker commands, CSS anchor positioning), server-rendered without hydration. Style them with your own CSS or the optional default theme.

**Status:** in development. `@lumiose/ui` keeps its own 0.x versions, apart from the version all
other Lumiose packages share, and is not on npm yet: today it is used from this repository's
workspace. The goal for its 1.0 is parity with [Base UI](https://base-ui.com)'s components; the
table below lists them as they land.

These pages ship in the package, in `node_modules/@lumiose/ui/docs`, so they match the installed
version. For coding agents, `llms.txt` indexes them and `llms-full.txt` holds them all;
`lumiose docs ui` and `lumiose docs dialog` print them; the MCP server's `ui_components` tool lists
every component's parts, props, events and styling hooks; and `lumiose agents init` adds a UI
section to `AGENTS.md` and the `lumiose-ui` skill. Every component page has the same sections:
Anatomy, API, Example, Styling, Keyboard and focus, Without JavaScript, Browser support and Related.

## Approach

- **Native first.** A component renders the element the platform already has for the job: a
  `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command, a popover, a `<button>`. Those work in server HTML
  before any script loads, and keep the browser's own keyboard handling and focus management.
- **Custom elements only where the platform falls short.** Keyboard navigation in a menu or the
  filtering of a combobox need script: those components render a light-DOM custom element with a
  `lu-` tag (`lu-menu`, `lu-combobox`) that upgrades the server HTML in place. A page is meant to
  load only the definitions of the elements it renders, and no island runtime for them (in
  development, with those components).
- **Small scripts for native gaps.** Where a native element falls short of Base UI's behaviour, a
  small script closes the gap, such as Dialog's right-click and touch handling. The component
  still works without it; a page that renders the component loads it once, without the island
  runtime.
- **Parts.** Each component is a set of parts named as in Base UI (`Dialog.Root`,
  `Dialog.Trigger`, `Dialog.Popup`, …). Every part that renders an element takes that element's
  props (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, events) and passes them through.
- **Signals.** A component's state is a prop and a callback: `open` with `onOpenChange`, `checked`
  with `onCheckedChange`, `value` with `onValueChange`. Pass a signal's value and write it back in
  the callback to keep both in sync, or leave both out and the element keeps its own state. Custom
  elements report changes with lowercase DOM events, like native ones: `openchange`,
  `checkedchange` and `change`.
- **Keyboard contracts.** Every component follows its WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern, and
  its end-to-end tests check the keyboard paths.
- **WCAG 2.2 AA.** Every component meets it: the components own semantics, keyboard and
  behaviour, and the default theme owns the visual criteria (contrast, non-text contrast, focus
  visible, target size). Each component's end-to-end tests run axe with the WCAG A and AA rules,
  closed and open, in light and dark, and check reflow at 320 CSS pixels and text spacing.

This is the approach of [Timeless](https://timeless.build), ported to Lumiose.

## Styling

`@lumiose/ui` is **unstyled**: its stylesheets hold only what a component needs to work
(display, positioning and anchoring, the top layer, the CSS variables a component sets), in the
`lu.core` cascade layer. A look is opt-in: the default theme, or your own CSS.

```ts
import "@lumiose/ui/styles.css"; // what every component needs (or "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css", …)
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

Both stylesheets declare the layers `lu.core, lu.theme`, in that order. CSS outside layers always
wins over layered CSS, so your own stylesheets override the package's without specificity games.
If your app orders its own layers, put `lu` first: `@layer lu, reset, components;`.

### The default theme

`@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css` is a ready look for demos, prototypes and getting started: neutral
surfaces, a blue primary, light and dark. It styles a few classes, which you put on the parts
through their `class` prop:

| Class         | On                  | Variants                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lu-button`   | any `<button>` part | `data-variant="primary"`, `data-variant="destructive"`                  |
| `lu-dialog`   | `Dialog.Popup`      | Styles the backdrop, the title, the description and a `<footer>` inside |
| `lu-popover`  | `Popover.Popup`     | Styles the title, the description and a `<footer>` inside               |
| `lu-tooltip`  | `Tooltip.Popup`     |                                                                         |
| `lu-tabs`     | `Tabs.Root`         | Styles the list, the tabs (the selected one underlined) and the panels  |
| `lu-menu`     | every `Menu.Popup`  | Styles the items, their checkbox and radio marks, separators and labels |
| `lu-combobox` | `Combobox.Root`     | Lays out the field (label, chips, input, buttons) and styles the popup  |
| `lu-select`   | `Select.Root`       | Makes it a customizable select and styles the control and the picker    |

Its colours and radius are custom properties with shadcn/ui's names and a `--lu-` prefix, so a
shadcn palette carries over:

| Property                                          | Used for                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `--lu-background`, `--lu-foreground`              | Page-level surfaces and text        |
| `--lu-card`, `--lu-card-foreground`               | Cards                               |
| `--lu-popover`, `--lu-popover-foreground`         | Dialogs, popovers, menus            |
| `--lu-primary`, `--lu-primary-foreground`         | Primary actions                     |
| `--lu-secondary`, `--lu-secondary-foreground`     | Secondary actions                   |
| `--lu-muted`, `--lu-muted-foreground`             | Subdued surfaces and text           |
| `--lu-accent`, `--lu-accent-foreground`           | Hover and highlighted items         |
| `--lu-destructive`, `--lu-destructive-foreground` | Destructive actions                 |
| `--lu-border`, `--lu-input`, `--lu-ring`          | Borders, field borders, focus rings |
| `--lu-radius`                                     | Corner radius                       |

The theme sets `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` and every colour with `light-dark()`, so it
follows the system. Set `color-scheme: light` (or `dark`) on `:root` or on any element to force
one, and redefine a property outside layers to change it:

```css
:root {
  --lu-primary: #7c3aed;
  --lu-radius: 0.375rem;
}
```

The theme meets WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark: each `-foreground` colour reaches 4.5:1 on its
surface, and `--lu-input` (the borders of fields and controls) and `--lu-ring` (the focus ring)
reach 3:1 on the surfaces they sit on. `--lu-border` is for decoration, such as a dialog's edge:
it is too light to outline a control. Keep those ratios when you change the colours.

### Your own CSS

Style the parts through:

- **Class props.** Every part takes `class` (and `style`), like the element it renders. No part
  carries a class or attribute of its own.
- **State.** Components expose state the way the platform does, so selectors read it directly:
  `dialog[open]`, `:modal`, `::backdrop`, `:popover-open`, `[aria-expanded]`, `[aria-checked]`,
  `[aria-selected]`, and `data-highlighted` on the active option of a list.

Each component's page has an example stylesheet to start from.

## Components

| Component                         | Status                                                                |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Dialog, alert dialog](dialog.md) | Available: native `<dialog>`, works without JavaScript                |
| [Popover](popover.md)             | Available: native popover, works without JavaScript                   |
| [Tooltip](tooltip.md)             | Available: native hint popover, opened by its script                  |
| [Menu](menu.md)                   | Available: popover menu, opens without JavaScript                     |
| [Combobox](combobox.md)           | Available: `<lu-combobox>`, a form control that filters its options   |
| [Select](select.md)               | Available: native `<select>`, customizable where supported, no script |
| [Tabs](tabs.md)                   | Available: server HTML with the full state, `<lu-tabs>` adds the keys |

## Size

`@lumiose/ui` is opt-in, so its size is reported apart from the runtime's caps:
`pnpm --filter @lumiose/ui size` prints, per component, the JavaScript a server-rendered page loads
for its custom elements, the JavaScript an island that uses it loads, and its CSS (minified, gzip
and brotli).

## Related

- [Web components](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/guides/web-components/): custom elements in Lumiose pages and islands.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): where components run in the browser.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `class`, events and `on:`.

<!-- source: combobox.md -->

# Combobox

> A text input that filters a list of options, for picking one value or several from many: the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete, after Base UI's Combobox. The input shows the option's label and the form gets its value. `<lu-combobox>`, a 3.8 kB form-associated light-DOM element, runs it on server-rendered pages and in islands; `bind:value` and `bind:open` keep signals in sync. Groups, an empty state, a status, a clear button, multiple values with chips, validation and async options.

```ts
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/combobox"
import "@lumiose/ui/combobox.css"; // places the popup and keeps filtered options hidden
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Combobox.Root>
  <Combobox.Label />
  <Combobox.Chips />
  <Combobox.Input />
  <Combobox.Clear />
  <Combobox.Trigger />
  <Combobox.Popup>
    <Combobox.List>
      <Combobox.Item />
      <Combobox.Group>
        <Combobox.GroupLabel />
        <Combobox.Item />
      </Combobox.Group>
    </Combobox.List>
    <Combobox.Empty />
    <Combobox.Status />
  </Combobox.Popup>
</Combobox.Root>
```

| Part         | Renders                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`       | `<lu-combobox>`, a form control with no box (`display: contents`) that holds the value and runs the parts.                                      |
| `Label`      | `<label for="…">` for the input; it also names the listbox.                                                                                     |
| `Input`      | `<input type="text" role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-expanded="…" aria-controls="…" autocomplete="off">`, the anchor of the popup. |
| `Trigger`    | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" command="--toggle" commandfor="…">`, which opens and closes the popup.                                     |
| `Clear`      | `<button type="button" tabindex="-1" command="--clear" commandfor="…">`, hidden while there is nothing to clear.                                |
| `Chips`      | `<div role="list">` of the selected values, with `multiple`; the script renders a `<span role="listitem">` for each, with a remove `<button>`.  |
| `Popup`      | `<div popover="manual" data-side="…" data-align="…">` around the `List`, for an empty state or a status beside it. Optional.                    |
| `List`       | `<div role="listbox">` of options; the popover itself (`popover="manual"`, `data-side`, `data-align`) when there is no `Popup`.                 |
| `Item`       | `<div role="option" data-value="…" aria-selected="…">`.                                                                                         |
| `Group`      | `<div role="group">` of options, named by its `GroupLabel`, hidden while none of its options matches.                                           |
| `GroupLabel` | `<div role="presentation">`, which names its `Group`.                                                                                           |
| `Empty`      | `<div role="status" hidden>`, shown instead of the options when none matches the text. Inside a `Popup`.                                        |
| `Status`     | `<div role="status">` for a message whose changes are announced, such as "Searching…". Inside a `Popup`, or anywhere in the `Root`.             |

Every part goes inside `Root`. Options and groups go inside the `List`; the `Empty` and `Status`
parts go next to it in a `Popup`, never inside the listbox.

## API

### Combobox.Root

| Prop            | Type                                   | Default      |                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`, `string[]` with `multiple`   |              | Selects the option with this value (these values) when it changes. `""` or `[]` selects nothing.                            |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`, `string[]` with `multiple`   |              | The selection at first, when `value` is left out.                                                                           |
| `onValueChange` | `(value) => void`                      |              | Called after the user chooses, removes or clears a value, with the new value. Typing never calls it.                        |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`, `Signal<string[]>`   |              | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                                                                  |
| `open`          | `boolean`                              |              | Opens or closes the popup when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed.                                |
| `onOpenChange`  | `(open: boolean) => void`              |              | Called after the popup opens or closes, whatever did it.                                                                    |
| `bind:open`     | `Signal<boolean>`                      |              | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                    |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | Several values: choosing an option toggles it and the popup stays open. `value` is then an array.                           |
| `name`          | `string`                               |              | The name the value is submitted under; with `multiple`, each value is its own entry.                                        |
| `required`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | The form needs a value: the browser reports an empty combobox at its input on submit.                                       |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                              | `false`      | The input and the buttons are disabled. A disabled `<fieldset>` around it does the same.                                    |
| `filter`        | `"contains" \| "startsWith" \| "none"` | `"contains"` | How typing filters the options by their label, ignoring case and accents. `"none"` leaves filtering to you (async options). |

Without `value`, `onValueChange` or `bind:value` the combobox keeps its own state. `Root` passes
`class`, `style` and other element props to `<lu-combobox>`.

### Combobox.Item

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`    | `string`  |         | Required: the value the combobox takes, and submits, when the option is chosen.        |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | The text the input shows and typing matches, when the option's text content is not it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | The option cannot be chosen, and the arrow keys skip it (`aria-disabled`).             |

### Combobox.List and Combobox.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default    |                                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"` | The input's side the popup goes on. It flips when it does not fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"start"`  | How the popup aligns with the input along that side.               |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |            | The gap between the input and the popup, in CSS pixels.            |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |            | A shift along the side, away from the aligned edge, in CSS pixels. |

The placement props go on the part that is the popover: the `Popup` when there is one, else the
`List`.

### Combobox.Chips

| Prop          | Type     | Default    |                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `removeLabel` | `string` | `"Remove"` | The remove buttons' name, before the value's label: "Remove Berlin". |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`tabindex`,
`autocomplete`, `hidden`); the roles, ids, ARIA references, commands and the anchor stay the parts'
own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Input`**: `placeholder`, `onInput` (for async options) and `aria-describedby` pass through.
  Its `type` and `value` are the combobox's.
- **`Trigger`** and **`Clear`**: out of the tab order, as in the APG examples; the input does
  everything from the keyboard. Name them with `aria-label` (or content).
- **`Group`**: `aria-labelledby` points at its `GroupLabel` while one renders.

**Differences from Base UI's Combobox.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop`, `Arrow`, `Value`,
`Icon`, `ItemIndicator`, `Row`, `Collection` or `Separator`: the top layer and anchor positioning
replace the first ones, and the theme draws the selected mark from `[aria-selected="true"]`. The
options are markup, not an `items` array, and filtering compares their labels; `filter="none"`
hands it to you, as Base UI's `filter={null}`. The chips are rendered by the script from the
selected options' labels rather than by your components, so a server-rendered page needs no island
for them. `Label` is a part of its own (Base UI uses `Field.Label`). Arrow keys skip disabled
options, as in Zag.

## Example

A city picker in a server-rendered page, with no island, in a form:

```tsx check
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui";

const CITIES = [
  { value: "ber", label: "Berlin" },
  { value: "lis", label: "Lisbon" },
  { value: "mad", label: "Madrid" },
];

export function CityField() {
  return (
    <form method="post">
      <Combobox.Root name="city" defaultValue="lis" required class="lu-combobox">
        <Combobox.Label>City</Combobox.Label>
        <Combobox.Input placeholder="Search cities" />
        <Combobox.Clear aria-label="Clear city" />
        <Combobox.Trigger aria-label="Show cities" />
        <Combobox.Popup>
          <Combobox.List>
            {CITIES.map((city) => (
              <Combobox.Item value={city.value}>{city.label}</Combobox.Item>
            ))}
          </Combobox.List>
          <Combobox.Empty>No city matches.</Combobox.Empty>
        </Combobox.Popup>
      </Combobox.Root>
      <button class="lu-button">Save</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

In an island: several values bound to a signal, and options loaded as the user types.
`bind:value={tags}` is short for `value={tags()}` plus `onValueChange={(next) => tags.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Combobox } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function TagPicker(props: { search: (text: string) => Promise<string[]> }) {
  const tags = signal<string[]>([]);
  const results = signal<string[]>([]);
  const searching = signal(false);
  const search = async (text: string) => {
    searching.set(true);
    results.set(await props.search(text));
    searching.set(false);
  };
  return (
    <Combobox.Root multiple name="tags" filter="none" bind:value={tags} class="lu-combobox">
      <Combobox.Label>Tags</Combobox.Label>
      <Combobox.Chips />
      <Combobox.Input
        onInput={(event) => search((event.currentTarget as HTMLInputElement).value)}
      />
      <Combobox.Popup>
        <Combobox.List>
          {results().map((tag) => (
            <Combobox.Item value={tag}>{tag}</Combobox.Item>
          ))}
        </Combobox.List>
        <Combobox.Status>{searching() ? "Searching…" : ""}</Combobox.Status>
      </Combobox.Popup>
    </Combobox.Root>
  );
}
```

With `filter="none"`, the script gives new options the selection and opens the popup when results
arrive while the user types; a chosen value keeps its label after its option is gone.

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-combobox` on `Root`. It turns the root into the field's grid
(the label, the chips, then the input with the trigger and clear buttons over its inline end, with
a glyph when they are empty), and styles the popup, the options (highlighted, selected with a ✓,
disabled), the group labels, the chips and the empty and status messages. Its colours come from the
theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)), and it sets a 4px gap
with `--lu-side-offset`.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state:

- the input: `[aria-expanded="true"]` while the popup is open, `[aria-invalid="true"]` after a
  submit found it empty, `:disabled`;
- the popup: `:popover-open`, `data-side` and `data-align`;
- options: `[data-highlighted]` on the active option (by keyboard or pointer; focus stays in the
  input), `[aria-selected="true"]`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`;
- `[role="group"]`, a group label's `[role="presentation"]`, `[role="status"]`;
- chips: `[role="listitem"]` in the `Chips` list, and its `button`;
- the buttons: `[command="--toggle"]`, `[command="--clear"]` (`[hidden]` while there is nothing to
  clear);
- the element: `lu-combobox:disabled`, `:invalid` and `:user-invalid` (it is a form control).

A starting point:

```css
.combobox [role="listbox"] {
  max-block-size: 18rem;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  --lu-side-offset: 4px;
}
.combobox [role="option"] {
  padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
}
.combobox [role="option"][data-highlighted] {
  background: #f4f4f5;
  outline: 2px solid #2563eb;
  outline-offset: -2px;
}
.combobox [role="option"][aria-selected="true"]::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/combobox.css` holds what the combobox needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer:
`lu-combobox` has no box, the options, groups and empty state the script hides stay hidden whatever
`display` your CSS gives them, and the shared placement rules anchor the popup to the input (with
CSS anchor positioning, a popup sits on its `data-side` and `data-align`, keeps the gaps of
`--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`, and flips when it does not fit).

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) with a listbox
popup, list autocomplete and manual selection, with Base UI's behaviour where it leaves a choice.
Focus stays in the input; the active option is `aria-activedescendant`.

| Key                  | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A character          | Edits the text, filters the options and opens the popup when something matches (or there is an `Empty`). Never commits.                                                                             |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up | Closed: opens the popup on the selected option, else the first (Arrow Up: the last). Open: the next or previous option, past the last back to the input, then around. Disabled options are skipped. |
| Alt+Arrow Down       | Opens the popup without highlighting an option.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Alt+Arrow Up         | Closes the popup.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Enter                | Chooses the highlighted option. With nothing highlighted, it does what Enter does in a form field.                                                                                                  |
| Escape               | Closes the popup without choosing and puts the selection's label back. Closed, it goes on to the page, so a dialog closes.                                                                          |
| Tab                  | Closes the popup without choosing and moves on.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Backspace            | With `multiple`, in an empty input: removes the last value.                                                                                                                                         |
| Home, End            | Move the text cursor, as in any text field.                                                                                                                                                         |

- **Choosing** an option puts its label in the input and closes the popup, or, with `multiple`,
  toggles it, clears the text and keeps the popup open. It fires `change` once per change.
- **Emptying the input** clears a single selection. Closing the popup without choosing (Escape,
  Tab, a click outside) puts the label back.
- **The pointer**: a click on the input opens the popup, hovering highlights an option, a click
  chooses it; presses in the popup and on the buttons keep focus in the input. A click outside
  closes the popup; a right-click or a second finger outside leaves it open, as in Base UI.
- **IME**: while composing, Enter and the arrows belong to the input method.

## Without JavaScript, and the element's script

The combobox needs its script: there is no native element that filters a styled list (`<datalist>`
cannot be styled or grouped, and customizable select cannot filter). Without JavaScript the server
HTML shows a labelled text field and nothing opens, and the form gets no value. For a choice that
must work without JavaScript, use [Select](select.md).

A page that renders a `Combobox` loads the script once, as a 3.8 kB (brotli) module without the
Lumiose runtime, and islands bundle it. It defines `lu-combobox`, which upgrades every combobox on
the page in place: it reads the selection the server rendered (`aria-selected="true"`), puts its
label in the input, renders the chips, and from then on owns the value, the filtering, the popup,
the keyboard and the form value. Its popup is a manual popover, dismissed by the model Menu and
Popover share: an outside press with the main button, a close request (Escape, the Android back
gesture), Tab, or focus moving elsewhere.

The element is also an API of its own, for scripts and other frameworks:

- `value`: the selected option's `data-value` (`""` for none), or an array with `multiple`;
  setting it selects without a `change` event.
- `open`: a property; setting it opens or closes the popup.
- `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `multiple`: reflect their attributes; `filter` is an attribute.
- `form`, `validity`, `validationMessage`, `willValidate`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`:
  as on native controls. It submits under `name`, resets with its form and follows a disabled
  `<fieldset>`.
- `change`: a bubbling event after the user chooses, removes or clears a value. The inner input's
  own `change` stays inside.
- `openchange`: an event (not bubbling, like `toggle`) with `detail.open`, after the popup opens or
  closes.
- The buttons are invoker commands: a `<button commandfor="<the element's id>" command="--toggle">`
  (or `"--clear"`) works anywhere on the page; where the browser lacks invoker commands, the
  element handles the clicks of those inside it.

## Browser support

- **Form-associated custom elements** (`ElementInternals`): Chrome and Edge 77, Firefox 98,
  Safari 16.4.
- **Popovers**: Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17. **`showPopover({ source })`**: Chrome
  137, Firefox 144, Safari 26; older browsers open the popup the same way.
- **CSS anchor positioning** places the popup: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26 (partly;
  27 fully). Elsewhere the script places it with the same sides, alignment, offsets and flips.
- **Invoker commands**: Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2; elsewhere the element handles the
  buttons' clicks.
- **`CloseWatcher`**, for the Android back gesture: Chrome 126, Firefox 149. Elsewhere Escape still
  closes the popup.

## Related

- [Select](select.md): a native select, when the user picks from a short list without typing; it
  works without JavaScript.
- [Menu](menu.md): commands rather than values, and the dismissal model the combobox shares.
- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `bind:value`, `bind:open` and async options.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:`, native events with `on:` and
  `ref`.

<!-- source: dialog.md -->

# Dialog

> A modal dialog, or an alert dialog that needs an answer: a native `<dialog>` opened and closed by invoker commands, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 0.8 kB script closes the native element's gaps where JavaScript runs. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/dialog"
import "@lumiose/ui/dialog.css"; // locks the page's scroll behind a modal dialog
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Dialog.Root>
  <Dialog.Trigger />
  <Dialog.Popup>
    <Dialog.Title />
    <Dialog.Description />
    <Dialog.Close />
  </Dialog.Popup>
</Dialog.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share.                                                                |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" command="show-modal" commandfor="…" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="…">`                         |
| `Popup`       | `<dialog closedby="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`; `role="alertdialog"` for an alert dialog |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the dialog.                                                                                               |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                                    |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" command="close" commandfor="…">`: its `value` becomes the dialog's `returnValue`.                      |

The trigger can sit anywhere inside `Root`, and a popup may have several close buttons. `Title` and
`Description` go inside `Popup`. A dialog may contain another `Dialog.Root`: the inner dialog
opens on top of the outer one.

## API

### Dialog.Root

| Prop           | Type                        | Default    |                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                   |            | Opens or closes the dialog when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a modal dialog opens only from a trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void`   |            | Called after the dialog opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside or `open`.                         |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`           |            | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the dialog, and follows it.                                                  |
| `role`         | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` | `"dialog"` | `"alertdialog"` for a confirmation that needs an answer: a click outside does not close it.                                                       |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the dialog keeps its own state.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`,
`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `closedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`); `id`,
`command` and `commandfor` stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` follows the dialog in the browser. In server HTML it stays
  `"false"`, which is never wrong where assistive technology can reach it: while the modal dialog
  is open, the trigger is inert.
- **`Popup`**: `closedby` is `"any"` for a dialog (Escape or a click outside closes it) and
  `"closerequest"` for an alert dialog (Escape only); pass `closedby="none"` to allow neither. Native
  events work as on a `<dialog>`: `on:close` runs after any close, and
  `event.currentTarget.returnValue` holds the value of the `Close` that closed it (it is unchanged
  after Escape).
- **`Title`** and **`Description`**: the popup's `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` point at
  the ones it renders, and only those; in an island they follow parts that appear or go away. A
  dialog without a `Title` needs an `aria-label` on `Popup`.

## Example

A confirmation in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root role="alertdialog">
      <Dialog.Trigger class="lu-button">Delete project…</Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Popup class="lu-dialog">
        <Dialog.Title>Delete project?</Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>This removes the project and its deployments.</Dialog.Description>
        <footer>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" value="cancel">
            Cancel
          </Dialog.Close>
          <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="destructive" value="delete">
            Delete
          </Dialog.Close>
        </footer>
      </Dialog.Popup>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: the button outside opens it, and the signal follows whatever
closes it. `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`.

```tsx check
import { Dialog } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditProfile() {
  const open = signal(false);
  const saved = signal("");
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" class="lu-button" onClick={() => open.set(true)}>
        Edit profile
      </button>
      <Dialog.Root bind:open={open}>
        <Dialog.Popup
          class="lu-dialog"
          on:close={(event) => saved.set(event.currentTarget.returnValue)}
        >
          <Dialog.Title>Edit profile</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description>Your name as others see it.</Dialog.Description>
          <footer>
            <Dialog.Close class="lu-button" data-variant="primary" value="save">
              Save
            </Dialog.Close>
          </footer>
        </Dialog.Popup>
      </Dialog.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Editing…" : `Last answer: ${saved() || "none"}`}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-dialog` on `Popup` and `lu-button` on the buttons
(`data-variant="primary"` or `"destructive"` for filled ones). `lu-dialog` also styles the backdrop,
the title, the description and a `<footer>` for the buttons, and fades and zooms the dialog in and
out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and the dialog's native state: `dialog[open]`,
`:modal`, `::backdrop` and `[role="alertdialog"]`. Where the client script runs, a dialog with open
dialogs inside also gets `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` (how many are open inside
it), as in Base UI; `dialog:has(dialog[open])` matches the same dialogs without the script. A starting point, with a fade that keeps the dialog in the top layer while it
closes:

```css
.dialog {
  inline-size: min(28rem, 100vw - 2rem);
  padding: 1.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.75rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
.dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .dialog,
  .dialog::backdrop {
    transition:
      opacity 150ms ease-out,
      overlay 150ms allow-discrete,
      display 150ms allow-discrete;
  }
  .dialog:not([open]),
  .dialog:not([open])::backdrop {
    opacity: 0;
  }
  @starting-style {
    .dialog[open],
    .dialog[open]::backdrop {
      opacity: 0;
    }
  }
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/dialog.css` holds one rule, in the `lu.core` layer: the page behind any modal
`<dialog>` does not scroll, and keeps its scrollbar's space so the layout does not shift
(`:root:has(dialog:modal) { overflow: hidden; scrollbar-gutter: stable }`). Leave the stylesheet out,
or override the rule, to let the page scroll.

## Keyboard and focus

The browser's modal dialog provides the
[WAI-ARIA dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/):

| Key            | Does                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space   | On the trigger: opens the dialog.                                                                    |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Move between the focusable elements of the dialog. The page behind is inert: focus never reaches it. |
| Escape         | Closes the dialog on top, alert dialogs included. With nested dialogs, one Escape closes one dialog. |

- **On open**, focus moves to the element with `autofocus`, or else the first focusable element
  inside, or else the dialog. Opened by touch, the dialog focuses itself instead, so no virtual
  keyboard opens over it (an `autofocus` element still gets focus).
- **On close**, focus returns to the element that had it before: the trigger, or the button that
  set the signal. If that element is gone, focus goes to another trigger of the dialog, without
  scrolling the page.
- **A click outside** closes a dialog, not an alert dialog, and only the dialog on top. A press
  that starts inside and ends outside, such as selecting text, does not count, and neither does a
  right-click or a second finger.
- Popups opened from a dialog (a menu, a select) belong inside its `Popup`: everything outside a
  modal dialog is inert.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape and the click outside are HTML features: a dialog in a
server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none. `open`, `onOpenChange`,
`bind:open` and a live `aria-expanded` need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

Where the native element falls short of Base UI's dialog, a small script closes the gap: a page
that renders a `Dialog` loads it once, as a 0.8 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and
islands bundle it. It covers every `<dialog>` on the page:

- a right-click or a second finger outside does not close the dialog;
- `data-nested-dialog-open` and `--nested-dialogs` on a dialog with open dialogs inside;
- a dialog opened by touch focuses itself;
- focus returns without scrolling, to the opener or, if it is gone, another trigger (WebKit, which
  does not focus a clicked button, would otherwise leave focus on the page);
- the click outside where the browser lacks `closedby` (Safari), and the invoker commands where it
  lacks them.

Until the script loads (or without JavaScript) the dialog behaves as the browser's own.

## Browser support

- **Invoker commands** (`command`, `commandfor`) open and close the dialog: Chrome and Edge 135,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26.2. In older browsers the client script stands in for them; without
  JavaScript the trigger and the close buttons do nothing there.
- **`closedby`**: Chrome 134 and Firefox 141; Safari only in Technology Preview. Elsewhere the
  client script closes the dialog on a click outside; without JavaScript only Escape does.
- **Exit animations** that keep the dialog in the top layer (`overlay`) are Chromium-only.
  Elsewhere the dialog leaves the top layer as soon as it starts closing.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the browser, for `open` and
  `onOpenChange`.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): native events with `on:` and `ref`.

<!-- source: menu.md -->

# Menu

> A menu of commands, links, checkbox and radio items and submenus, opened by a button: the trigger's `popovertarget` opens it and CSS anchor positioning places it, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript, and a 3.3 kB script adds the APG Menu Button keyboard contract where JavaScript runs. `bind:open`, `bind:checked` and `bind:value` keep signals in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/menu"
import "@lumiose/ui/menu.css"; // places the popup next to its trigger and stacks the items
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Popup>
    <Menu.Item />
    <Menu.LinkItem />
    <Menu.CheckboxItem />
    <Menu.Separator />
    <Menu.Group>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.Item />
    </Menu.Group>
    <Menu.RadioGroup>
      <Menu.GroupLabel />
      <Menu.RadioItem />
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
    <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      <Menu.SubmenuTrigger />
      <Menu.Popup>…</Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
  </Menu.Popup>
</Menu.Root>
```

| Part             | Renders                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`           | `<lu-menu>`, an element with no box (`display: contents`) that holds the menu's state and adds the keyboard contract.                                |
| `Trigger`        | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`; `aria-expanded` follows the menu once the script runs.                              |
| `Popup`          | `<div role="menu" popover="auto" tabindex="-1" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, labelled by its trigger; `popover="manual"` once the script opens it. |
| `Item`           | `<button type="button" role="menuitem">`: a command.                                                                                                 |
| `LinkItem`       | `<a role="menuitem">`: a link.                                                                                                                       |
| `CheckboxItem`   | `<button type="button" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="…">`                                                                                    |
| `Separator`      | `<div role="separator">`                                                                                                                             |
| `Group`          | `<div role="group">`, labelled by its `GroupLabel`.                                                                                                  |
| `GroupLabel`     | `<div role="presentation">`, which names its `Group` or `RadioGroup`.                                                                                |
| `RadioGroup`     | `<div role="group">` of radio items, one of them checked.                                                                                            |
| `RadioItem`      | `<button type="button" role="menuitemradio" value="…" aria-checked="…">`                                                                             |
| `SubmenuRoot`    | `<lu-menu>` for a submenu, inside a `Popup`.                                                                                                         |
| `SubmenuTrigger` | `<button type="button" role="menuitem" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="menu">`: an item of the parent menu.                                         |

The trigger and the popup sit inside `Root`; a submenu's trigger and popup sit inside its
`SubmenuRoot`, which sits in the parent's `Popup`, as deep as you like. Items, groups and separators
go inside a `Popup`, radio items inside a `RadioGroup`.

## API

### Menu.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the menu when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a popover opens only from its trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the menu opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a key, a click outside, an item that ran, `open`.                       |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`: the signal opens and closes the menu, and follows it.                                               |

Without `open`, `onOpenChange` or `bind:open` the menu keeps its own state. A menu opened from the
server HTML before its island hydrated stays open, and `onOpenChange(true)` tells the signal.
`Menu.SubmenuRoot` takes the same props, for its submenu.

### Menu.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default                                 |                                                                      |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"`, `"inline-end"` in a submenu | The trigger's side the popup goes on. It flips when it does not fit. |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"start"`                               | How the popup aligns with the trigger along that side.               |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   |                                         | The gap between the trigger and the popup, in CSS pixels.            |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   |                                         | A shift along the side, away from the aligned edge, in CSS pixels.   |

### Menu.Item

| Prop           | Type                          | Default |                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onClick`      | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |         | Runs the command, on a click, Enter or Space. The menu has closed and focus is back on the trigger by then. |
| `disabled`     | `boolean`                     | `false` | Unavailable (`aria-disabled`): the arrows and typeahead still reach it, but it does not run.                |
| `label`        | `string`                      |         | The text typeahead matches, when the item's text content is not it.                                         |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean`                     | `true`  | Whether running the item closes the menu.                                                                   |

### Menu.LinkItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`         | `string`  |         | Where the link goes. A Ctrl, Cmd or Shift click, or a link with `download`, leaves the menu open.                                                                            |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `true`  | Whether following the link closes the menu. Base UI keeps it open by default; here it closes, like the other items, since a layout's menu outlives a client-side navigation. |

### Menu.CheckboxItem

| Prop              | Type                         | Default |                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                    |         | Checks or unchecks the item when it changes. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`. |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it starts checked when `checked` is left out.                        |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |         | Called after a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks it.                  |
| `bind:checked`    | `Signal<boolean>`            |         | Stands in for `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.                               |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                    | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it does not toggle.                  |
| `label`           | `string`                     |         | The text typeahead matches.                                                  |
| `closeOnClick`    | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether toggling it closes the menu.                                         |

### Menu.RadioGroup

| Prop            | Type                      | Default |                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                  |         | Checks the radio item with this `value` when it changes. Pair it with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                  |         | The radio item checked at first when `value` is left out.                              |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |         | Called with the `value` of the radio item a click, Enter or Space checks.              |
| `bind:value`    | `Signal<string>`          |         | Stands in for `value` and `onValueChange`.                                             |

### Menu.RadioItem

| Prop           | Type      | Default |                                                            |
| -------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `value`        | `string`  |         | Required: the value its group takes when it is checked.    |
| `disabled`     | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but it is not checked. |
| `label`        | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches.                                |
| `closeOnClick` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether checking it closes the menu.                       |

### Menu.SubmenuTrigger

| Prop       | Type      | Default |                                                                    |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Unavailable: it can be highlighted, but its submenu does not open. |
| `label`    | `string`  |         | The text typeahead matches in the parent menu.                     |

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`, `tabindex`,
`aria-labelledby`, `data-side`, `data-align`); the roles, `id`, `popovertarget` and the anchor
stay the parts' own, since they connect the parts. Your `style` is kept, after the anchor's.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` is left to the browser in server HTML, where `popovertarget`
  implies it, and set by the script once it runs. Disable it with the native `disabled`.
- **`Group`** and **`RadioGroup`**: `aria-labelledby` points at their `GroupLabel` while one
  renders; without one, give the group an `aria-label`.
- **`Separator`**: a horizontal rule between items; `aria-orientation` passes through.

**Differences from Base UI's Menu.** No `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Backdrop` or `Arrow`: the top
layer and anchor positioning replace them, and the placement props go on `Popup`. The menu is not
modal: the page keeps scrolling (the popup follows its trigger), and a press outside closes the
menu and reaches what it lands on. Items render buttons, so they run with Enter and Space without
the script. There are no indicator parts: style `[aria-checked="true"]`. Submenus open on hover
after 100 ms, which no prop changes, and the root trigger does not open on hover.

## Example

A menu in a server-rendered page, with no island, styled by the default theme:

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function ProjectMenu() {
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">Project</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/settings">Settings</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.LinkItem href="/members">Members</Menu.LinkItem>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.SubmenuRoot>
          <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>Export</Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
          <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu">
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.csv" download>
              CSV
            </Menu.LinkItem>
            <Menu.LinkItem href="/export.json" download>
              JSON
            </Menu.LinkItem>
          </Menu.Popup>
        </Menu.SubmenuRoot>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, with commands, a checkbox item and a radio group bound to signals.
`bind:checked={wrap}` is short for `checked={wrap()}` plus
`onCheckedChange={(next) => wrap.set(next)}`, and `bind:value` likewise.

```tsx check
import { Menu } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function EditorMenu(props: { onFormat: () => void }) {
  const wrap = signal(true);
  const indent = signal("spaces");
  return (
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger class="lu-button">View</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Popup class="lu-menu" align="end">
        <Menu.Item onClick={props.onFormat}>Format document</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Item disabled>Fold all</Menu.Item>
        <Menu.Separator />
        <Menu.CheckboxItem bind:checked={wrap}>Wrap lines</Menu.CheckboxItem>
        <Menu.RadioGroup bind:value={indent}>
          <Menu.GroupLabel>Indent with</Menu.GroupLabel>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="spaces">Spaces</Menu.RadioItem>
          <Menu.RadioItem value="tabs">Tabs</Menu.RadioItem>
        </Menu.RadioGroup>
      </Menu.Popup>
    </Menu.Root>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-menu` on every `Popup`, submenus included, and `lu-button` on
the trigger. `lu-menu` styles the surface, the items (highlighted, disabled, focus ring), the
checkbox and radio marks, the arrow of a submenu trigger, the separators and the group labels, and
fades the popup in and out. Its colours come from the theme's `--lu-` properties
([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)), and it sets a 4px gap with `--lu-side-offset`.

**With your own CSS**, style the parts through `class` and their state:

- the popup: `:popover-open`, `data-side` and `data-align` (where it was asked to go);
- the trigger and a submenu trigger: `[aria-expanded="true"]` while their menu is open;
- items: `[data-highlighted]` on the item that has focus (by keyboard or pointer),
  `:focus-visible`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`, and `[aria-checked="true"]` on checkbox and radio
  items;
- `[role="separator"]`, `[role="group"]` and a group label's `[role="presentation"]`.

A starting point:

```css
.menu {
  min-inline-size: 10rem;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
  --lu-side-offset: 4px;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"] {
  padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 0.25rem;
  background: none;
  font: inherit;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][data-highlighted] {
  background: #f4f4f5;
}
.menu [role^="menuitem"][aria-disabled="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
}
.menu [aria-checked="true"]::before {
  content: "✓" / "";
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/menu.css` holds what the menu needs to work, in the `lu.core` layer: `lu-menu` has
no box, and the popup and its groups lay the items out in a column (`display: grid`, items
`display: flex`). It imports the placement rules Menu shares with Popover and Tooltip: with CSS
anchor positioning, a popup sits on its `data-side` and `data-align`, keeps the gaps of
`--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`, flips when it does not fit (a submenu tries the other
side, then the other alignment, then below and above its trigger) and hides while its trigger is
scrolled out of view. The `sideOffset` and `alignOffset` props set those two properties on the
popup.

## Keyboard and focus

The [WAI-ARIA Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/), with
Base UI's behaviour where the pattern leaves a choice:

| Key                       | Does                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space              | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item. On an item: runs it, or checks it. On a submenu trigger: opens it. |
| Arrow Down, Arrow Up      | On the trigger: opens the menu on its first item, or on its last. In the menu: the next or previous item, looping.   |
| Home, End                 | The first or last item.                                                                                              |
| Arrow Right (Left in RTL) | On a submenu trigger: opens the submenu on its first item.                                                           |
| Arrow Left (Right in RTL) | In a submenu: closes it, back on its trigger.                                                                        |
| A character               | The next item whose text starts with it; characters typed within 750 ms add up, and Space among them is text.        |
| Escape                    | Closes one level: the submenu on top, or the menu. Focus goes back to its trigger.                                   |
| Tab, Shift+Tab            | Close the whole menu. Tab moves on from the trigger; Shift+Tab stays on it.                                          |

- **On open**, focus moves to the first item that can run (Arrow Up: the last one). Opened by a
  pointer, the popup itself takes focus and no item is highlighted until a key or the pointer
  picks one.
- **On close**, focus returns to the trigger without scrolling the page, after Escape, Tab, an
  item that ran or a click outside on nothing focusable; a click on a button or a field outside
  leaves focus there.
- **Running an item** closes the whole menu and returns focus before the item's `onClick` runs,
  so a handler that opens a dialog gets focus back on the trigger when it closes. Checkbox and
  radio items stay open.
- **Disabled items** (`aria-disabled`) stay in the arrow order and typeahead, as the pattern
  asks, but do not run.
- **The pointer** highlights the item under it, and leaving the items clears the highlight. A
  mouse press on the trigger opens the menu at once: releasing it on an item runs the item, and
  releasing it outside closes the menu. A submenu opens after the pointer rests 100 ms on its
  trigger, and stays open while the pointer heads for it across other items.
- **A click outside** closes the whole menu, submenus included, and a click in a menu closes the
  submenus open from it. A right-click, a middle click or a second finger outside leaves the menu
  open, as in Base UI.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger opens the popup with `popovertarget`, and Escape or a click outside closes it: a menu
in a server-rendered page opens before any script loads, and with none. Tab then moves through the
items in order, and links work; commands, which run JavaScript, need it anyway. `open`,
`onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props need the component to run in the browser, in an island.

The keyboard contract comes from a small script: a page that renders a `Menu` loads it once, as a
3.3 kB (brotli) module without the Lumiose runtime, and islands bundle it. It defines `lu-menu`,
which upgrades every menu on the page in place, and adds what the native popover lacks: focus on
open and its return on close, the arrows, Home, End and typeahead, Escape one level at a time, Tab,
submenus, checkbox and radio items, disabled items, `data-highlighted`, and the pointer behaviour
above. It also takes over dismissal, with the model Menu shares with [Popover](popover.md) and
[Combobox](combobox.md): the popup becomes a manual popover when the script opens it, and the
script closes it on a click outside (main button only), on Escape, on a close request such as the
Android back gesture, and when another popup opens outside it. Until it loads (or without JavaScript) the menu behaves as a
native `popover="auto"` of buttons, which any click outside closes.

The element is also an API of its own, for scripts and other frameworks:

- `open`: a property; setting it to `true` or `false` opens or closes the menu.
- `openchange`: an event (not bubbling, like `toggle`) with `detail.open`, after the menu opens or
  closes.
- `checkedchange`: a bubbling event that checkbox and radio items fire with `detail.checked` when
  a click, Enter or Space checks or unchecks them.

## Browser support

- **Popovers and `popovertarget`**: Chrome and Edge 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17.
- **CSS anchor positioning** places the popup: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26
  (partly; 27 fully). Elsewhere the client script places the popup with the same sides,
  alignment, offsets and flips; without JavaScript it shows where the browser shows any popover,
  in the middle of the viewport, and still works.
- **`showPopover({ source })`**, which ties a popup the script opens to its trigger: Chrome 137,
  Firefox 144, Safari 26. Older browsers open it the same way.
- **`CloseWatcher`**, for the Android back gesture: Chrome 126, Firefox 149. Elsewhere Escape
  still closes the menu.
- **Exit animations** that keep the popup in the top layer while it fades (`overlay`) are
  Chromium-only.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a menu item can open one; focus returns to the menu's trigger when it
  closes.
- [Islands](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/islands/): running a component in the
  browser, for `open`, `onOpenChange` and the `bind:` props.
- [JSX](https://itsjavi.com/lumiose/docs/concepts/jsx/): `bind:`, native events with `on:` and
  `ref`.

<!-- source: popover.md -->

# Popover

> A popup anchored to its trigger: a native `popover` opened and closed by the trigger's `popovertarget`, placed with CSS anchor positioning, so it works in server HTML with no JavaScript. A 1.7 kB script moves focus into it and back, dismisses it as Base UI does (not on a right-click), keeps `aria-expanded` current and places it in browsers without anchor positioning. `bind:open` (or `open` and `onOpenChange`) keeps a signal in sync in islands.

```ts
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui"; // or "@lumiose/ui/popover"
import "@lumiose/ui/popover.css"; // places the popup next to its trigger
import "@lumiose/ui/themes/default.css"; // optional: the default theme
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger />
  <Popover.Popup>
    <Popover.Title />
    <Popover.Description />
    <Popover.Close />
  </Popover.Popup>
</Popover.Root>
```

| Part          | Renders                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Root`        | No element. Holds the state and the ids the other parts share.                                                                                                              |
| `Trigger`     | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" aria-haspopup="dialog">`, with an `anchor-name` in its `style`.                                                                    |
| `Popup`       | `<div popover="auto" role="dialog" data-side="…" data-align="…">`, labelled by its `Title` and described by its `Description`; `popover="manual"` once the script opens it. |
| `Title`       | `<h2>`, which names the popup.                                                                                                                                              |
| `Description` | `<p>`, which describes it.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Close`       | `<button type="button" popovertarget="…" popovertargetaction="hide">`.                                                                                                      |

The popup is a non-modal dialog, as in Base UI: the page around it stays usable. A popover may
contain another `Popover.Root`: the inner popup opens on top, and closing the outer one closes
both.

## API

### Popover.Root

| Prop           | Type                      | Default |                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 |         | Opens or closes the popover when it changes, in the browser. Server HTML always starts closed: a popover opens only from its trigger or script. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |         | Called after the popover opens or closes, whatever did it: the trigger, a close button, Escape, a click outside, another popover or `open`.     |
| `bind:open`    | `Signal<boolean>`         |         | Stands in for `open` and `onOpenChange`.                                                                                                        |

### Popover.Popup

| Prop          | Type                                                                       | Default    |                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `side`        | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "right" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"bottom"` | The trigger's side the popup goes on. `inline-start` and `inline-end` follow `dir`.            |
| `align`       | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"`                                             | `"center"` | How the popup lines up with the trigger along that side.                                       |
| `sideOffset`  | `number`                                                                   | `0`        | The gap between the trigger and the popup, in CSS pixels.                                      |
| `alignOffset` | `number`                                                                   | `0`        | A shift along the side, in CSS pixels: away from the aligned edge, or right/down when centred. |

The popup flips to the opposite side when it does not fit, and goes below (or above) the trigger
when a `left` or `right` popup fits on neither side. It hides while its trigger is scrolled out
of view.

### The other parts

Each part takes the props of the element it renders (`class`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, event
handlers, `ref`) and passes them through. Your props override the defaults (`type`,
`aria-haspopup`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`); `id`, `popover` and
`popovertarget` stay the parts' own. A `style` you pass keeps the anchor name.

- **`Trigger`**: `aria-expanded` comes from the browser for `popovertarget`, and from the client
  script once it runs.
- **`Popup`**: native events work as on any popover: `on:toggle` and `on:beforetoggle`. A popup
  without a `Title` needs an `aria-label`.

## Example

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";

export function Notifications() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Notifications</Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" align="start">
        <Popover.Title>Notifications</Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>You are all caught up.</Popover.Description>
        <footer>
          <Popover.Close class="lu-button">Close</Popover.Close>
        </footer>
      </Popover.Popup>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

In an island, bound to a signal: `bind:open={open}` is short for `open={open()}` plus
`onOpenChange={(next) => open.set(next)}`. A popover opened by the signal still anchors to its
trigger and treats it as its invoker.

```tsx check
import { Popover } from "@lumiose/ui";
import { signal } from "lumiose";

export function Filters() {
  const open = signal(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Popover.Root bind:open={open}>
        <Popover.Trigger class="lu-button">Filters</Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup class="lu-popover" side="right" sideOffset={8}>
          <Popover.Title>Filters</Popover.Title>
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
      <p>{open() ? "Choosing filters…" : "All items"}</p>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

**With the default theme**, put `lu-popover` on `Popup`: a surface with the title, the
description and a `<footer>` styled, a 4px gap to the trigger, and a fade. Its colours come from the
theme's `--lu-` properties ([UI components](README.md#the-default-theme)).

**With your own CSS**, style the popup through `class` and its state: `:popover-open`,
`[data-side]` and `[data-align]` (the requested placement; a flip does not change them), and the
trigger through `[aria-expanded]`. Two custom properties set the offsets, and the props override
them: `--lu-side-offset` and `--lu-align-offset`.

```css
.popover {
  --lu-side-offset: 6px;
  padding: 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid #d4d4d8;
  border-radius: 0.5rem;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35);
}
```

`@lumiose/ui/popover.css` holds the placement, in the `lu.core` layer: for each `data-side` and
`data-align`, the CSS anchor positioning that puts the popup next to its trigger, with flips and
`position-visibility: anchors-visible`. Tooltip shares it.

## Keyboard and focus

| Key          | Does                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger: opens or closes the popover.                                                                                     |
| Tab          | Moves through the popup, then on to the element after the trigger. When the trigger is the last element, focus leaves the popup. |
| Shift+Tab    | From the start of the popup, back to the trigger. The popover stays open.                                                        |
| Escape       | Closes the popover on top. With nested popovers, or a popover in a dialog, one Escape closes one layer.                          |

- **On open**, focus moves to the first focusable element in the popup, or to the popup itself
  when it has none. Opened by touch, the popup focuses itself, so no virtual keyboard opens.
- **On close**, focus returns to the trigger without scrolling, unless a click outside landed on
  another control, which keeps it. Escape and the close buttons return it too.
- **A click outside** closes the popover; a right-click or a second finger does not. A press inside a nested popover does not close its
  parent, and opening another popover closes the first.
- Popovers opened from a dialog belong inside its `Popup`: everything outside a modal dialog is
  inert.

## Without JavaScript, and the client script

The trigger, the close buttons, Escape, the click outside and the placement are HTML and CSS
features: a popover in a server-rendered page works before any script loads, and with none.
`open`, `onOpenChange` and `bind:open` need the component to run in an island.

A page that renders a `Popover` loads a 1.7 kB (brotli) module once, without the Lumiose runtime;
islands bundle it. It covers every Popover on the page:

- focus on open (the first focusable element, or the popup) and its return on close;
- dismissal, shared with [Menu](menu.md) and [Combobox](combobox.md): a trigger's click makes the
  popup a manual popover, which the script closes on a click outside (main button only, so a
  right-click or a second finger does not close it, as in Base UI), on Escape and other close
  requests (the Android back gesture), and when another popover opens outside it. Until the
  script loads, the browser's light dismiss closes it on any press outside;
- `aria-expanded` on the triggers;
- the placement in browsers without CSS anchor positioning, which it keeps current on scroll and
  resize.

## Browser support

- **Popover and `popovertarget`**: every current browser (Baseline 2024).
- **CSS anchor positioning**: Chrome and Edge 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26. Elsewhere the client
  script places the popup; without JavaScript there it opens in the middle of the viewport.
- Safari and Firefox do not follow a trigger moved by a CSS `transform`.

## Related

- [UI components](README.md): the approach, styling, the default theme and the other components.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): a short tip on hover or focus, with the same placement props.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): a modal popup.

<!-- source: select.md -->

# Select

> A native `<select>` for picking one value from a list: it works with no JavaScript, submits with its form and keeps the platform's keyboard, typeahead and mobile pickers. Where the browser has customizable select (`appearance: base-select`, Chrome 135, Safari 27), `Select.Trigger` and `Select.Value` shape the button, the picker is styleable and options may hold more than text; elsewhere it is the classic select. No script; `bind:value` keeps a signal in sync in islands.

